authority_boundary.a1: identity backend, session transport, verification delivery, route facts
authority_boundary.a3: capability-aware product UI and public API reference

capabilities.request_requirement: Challenge start remains indistinguishable across eligible, unknown, blocked, unavailable, and exhausted outcomes.
capabilities.current_fact: A1 returns the same accepted public envelope and does not include challenge context.

capabilities.request_requirement: The browser receives a mailbox-bound short-lived context without raw identity scope.
capabilities.current_fact: Challenge start still omits challenge_id and no opaque verification context is issued to the browser.

capabilities.request_requirement: Verification resolves challenge, channel, identifier, purpose, and tenant from server-owned context.
capabilities.current_fact: The verify request still requires caller-provided challenge_id, channel, identifier, purpose, and tenant_id.

capabilities.request_requirement: Email may carry a short-lived signed single-use verification link or an equivalent secure flow cookie.
capabilities.current_fact: No verification_token or mailbox-link route is implemented in the current A1 baseline.

capabilities.request_requirement: Successful login or recovery verification creates or rotates a secure browser session.
capabilities.current_fact: A1 atomically completes verification, issues one-use access and refresh receipts, and writes Secure HttpOnly SameSite Strict cookies over trusted HTTPS.

capabilities.request_requirement: Browser sessions can rotate without exposing authorization material to A3.
capabilities.current_fact: The project-scoped refresh route requires HTTPS, same-origin browser context, idempotency, and paired cookie replacement.

capabilities.request_requirement: Successful verification returns a 303 redirect to an exact allowlisted webapp path.
capabilities.current_fact: Verification currently returns a 200 JSON result and has no allowlisted post-verify redirect contract.

capabilities.request_requirement: OAuth callback establishes the hosted browser session and redirects without exposing provider material.
capabilities.current_fact: The current compatibility baseline does not advertise an OAuth hosted-session redirect capability.

capabilities.request_requirement: A3 public API reference can rely on advertised A1 route facts.
capabilities.current_fact: The challenge and verify handlers dispatch, but neither route is listed in GoRouteManifestEntries.
